title: Race Comments
covers: Break at start; Wide; Boxed in; Eased; Lost rider event; Stretch run; closing kick
note: Equibase standardized chart-comment guide defines start comments, positioning/interference terms, Eased and Lost Jockey, and repeatedly uses stretch run as the finishing-stretch phase. It also defines lack of a final closing kick; keep North American chart-comment semantics scoped rather than universalizing labels.

title: Racing Explained — Glossary
covers: On the rail; Boxed in; Turn of foot
note: Current glossary directly defines Boxed In, running on/against the rails, and Turn Of Foot. Preserve British/Commonwealth wording and do not force worldwide synonym identity.

title: Overseas Racecard Starter Guide
note: HKJC official racecard guide lists LR = Lost rider separately from UR = Unseated rider, supporting a distinct result/event label in international race information.

title: Entries & Results Abbreviation Codes
note: Current USTA Chart Calls list X = Break, Boxed and Parked Out. Combined with existing USTA gait-rule evidence, Break is a regional label for the already modeled Broke stride Concept rather than a second semantic Concept.

title: Pace Makes the Race
note: Equibase's currently hosted pace-style explainer explicitly maps speed horses to front-runners/pacesetters, defines Presser as forcing the issue behind speed, and Stalker as sitting within striking range. Use to collapse generic Pacesetter into Front-runner and verify the two distinct North American style labels without treating the article's style taxonomy as universal.

title: Racetrack Experience — Position is Everything
note: Current USTA fan guide explains the pocket behind the leader on the rail, cover behind another horse, and a horse racing outside as parked/first-over. Use as North American Harness positioning terminology.

title: Current 2026 racebook / stewards-report terminology
covers: Midfield; Home turn; Carried wide; Tempo
note: Current 2026 Racing Australia racebook/stewards material uses midfield/mid-field as a race-position band, home turn as the final bend into the home straight, carried wider for a horse forced farther outside, and tempo for race pace. Treat these as Australian operational labels, not universal definitions.

title: Picking a Winner by Reading the Form
note: Current Jockey Club form guide states that R in jump-racing form indicates a horse refused. Use for the jump-racing non-completion event rather than the unrelated everyday sense of refuse.

title: Killarney 17th July 2026
note: Current IHRB stewards report uses run in for the section after the final hurdle and records a horse that ran out by going the wrong side of a wing and therefore taking the wrong course. Scope both terms to regulated GB/IRE jump-racing usage.

title: International Agreement on Trotting Races — 2025
covers: Gallop during trotting race; disqualification for gait
note: Article 6 requires the trotting gait and specifies mandatory or discretionary disqualification when a horse breaks stride into gallop/pace or uses irregular gait under stated conditions. Model Galloped as a gait-break event and Disqualified for gait as the decision outcome, not as ordinary flat-racing gallop terminology.
